title: Session anchoring and edge failover for progressive version rollouts
creator: Asha Patel
description: Problem: Progressive model rollouts (canary / A-B) interact unexpectedly with region/tier routing and request-level session state. Users observe inconsistent model affinity after failover, hot cache misses when traffic moves between variants, and increased tail latency when requests are bounced to fallback variants during capacity pressure. Goal: Implement a deterministic, observable session-anchoring mechanism combined with an edge failover policy that preserves rollout ratios, reduces cold-KV-cache penalties, and guarantees graceful degradation when preferred model variants are unavailable. Constraints: must work for hosted, dedicated, and private deployments; preserve per-customer isolation guarantees for Dedicated; be compatible with existing session pin TTL mechanisms and the orchestration layer's routing priority DAG. This ticket contains the design for runtime-level changes, the acceptance criteria, rollout plan, monitoring requirements, and integration points with console/rollout APIs.
acceptance_criteria: 1) New session-anchoring algorithm routes >=99.9% of session-bound requests to the pinned model variant while respecting canary split percentages for new sessions
2) Edge failover logic falls back to next-best variant within 50ms decision latency and records fallback events to the rollout dashboard
3) When a fallback occurs, a cache-warming hint is emitted so subsequent requests experience <=2x cold-cache latency at p99 compared to steady-state
4) Rollout controller can target canary traffic by session-creation probability or deterministic hashed cohort without violating per-region capacity constraints
5) Integration tests exercise region outage scenarios, capacity-constrained degraded paths, and sticky-session decay — all pass in CI
6) No user-visible regressions in latency SLOs (p99) or error rates during a staged rollout of this feature across one region and one Dedicated customer
technical_design: Overview: introduce a two-layer decision model: (A) session-anchoring resolver that decides binding (variant, pin-ttl, cohort) at session creation; (B) fast-path edge resolver that enforces variant affinity with ordered failover and records metrics.

Session creation: add deterministic hashing option (customer_id || session_id) -> cohort assignment. Cohort maps to rollout bucket (control/canary). If policy is probabilistic, the hashing is weighted by the configured canary percentage to remain stable across rebalances.

Pin TTL and decay: pinned sessions receive a configurable TTL (default 12h). To limit stale pins during long rollouts, implement exponential decay: after each TTL expiry, the session re-evaluates and probabilistically becomes unpinned with a decay rate derived from rollout velocity.

Edge failover ordering: resolver consults routing policy order: 1) exact pinned variant, 2) per-region compatible variant with same architecture/latency profile, 3) same-family quantized variant, 4) global fallback model. The resolver emits a decision trace and fallback_reason tag for visibility.

Cache-warming hint: when failover selects a variant absent from local KV cache, the edge attaches an async cache-warm hint (small warmed-prefix request) to the variant pool. Warm hints are rate-limited per-customer to avoid amplification.

Capacity-aware gating: the routing decision consults the capacity oracle and will probabilistically divert new session creations away from a canary if target pool saturation exceeds a threshold to protect SLOs.

Compatibility: new resolver is pluggable behind a feature flag. Dedicated customers may opt into a stricter pinning mode that prevents cross-variant fallbacks unless explicitly allowed by their policy.

Metrics and traces: emit per-request fields: session_id, cohort, pinned_variant, selected_variant, fallback_chain, decision_latency_ms. Aggregate rollout-level metrics for canary_exposure, fallback_rate, cache_warm_events, and per-variant p99 latency.
rollout_plan: 1) Implement feature-flagged resolver in runtime branch; unit tests + integration harness against the orchestrator simulator
2) Run canary within staging region for 48h with synthetic traffic (traffic sculpted to mimic customer session distributions), measure fallback_rate & cache-warm effectiveness
3) Gradually enable for 5% of traffic in a single production region (monitoring and rollback hooks), then 25% after 24h, then 100% for that region
4) Offer Dedicated customers opt-in via console toggle; coordinate with account teams for initial customers
5) Full cross-region enable after two successful regional rollouts and low fallback rates
6) Post-rollout: evaluate TTL decay parameters and tune based on observed session churn and canary exposure drift
test_plan: Unit tests for hash-to-cohort correctness and decay math
Integration tests: simulate region outage and assert fallback chain and metrics emitted
Load tests: ensure decision latency stays <50ms at peak qps and that cache-warm hints do not introduce amplification
E2E: end-to-end validation with runtime + orchestrator + console visualization for canary exposure and fallback events
Chaos experiments: node eviction and network partition to validate graceful degradation and rollback behavior
monitoring_and_alerting: Dashboards: rollout exposure by cohort/region, fallback_rate per-variant, cache_warm_success_rate, decision_latency p50/p95/p99
Alerts: fallback_rate > 1% sustained for 15m in a region -> SEV2 (investigate capacity mismatch or model error), decision_latency p99 > 200ms -> SEV3
SLO checks: ensure variant p99 latency delta vs baseline < 20% during rollout; automated rollback if delta > 25% for >30m
Audit logs: every session anchor and failover emits an audit event for Dedicated customers with retention configurable via console
